overview: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple, popularly known as Yadadri Temple or Yadagirigutta Temple, is one of the most revered Hindu temples dedicated to Lord Lakshmi Narasimha, the fourth incarnation of Lord Vishnu. Located atop a picturesque hill at Yadagirigutta in Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district of Telangana, it attracts millions of devotees every year and is regarded as one of the most important Vaishnavite pilgrimage centers in South India. Following a magnificent reconstruction inspired by traditional temple architecture, it is the spiritual pride of Telangana.
summary: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple, popularly known as Yadadri Temple, is one of the most sacred Narasimha temples in India. Located on a scenic hill in Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district, Telangana, the temple is associated with Sage Yadarishi and the divine appearance of Lord Narasimha in five forms. Following its grand reconstruction, Yadadri has emerged as one of India's finest pilgrimage destinations, attracting millions of devotees each year with its spiritual significance, magnificent architecture, and world-class facilities.

history.content: The temple's history is rooted in ancient Hindu scriptures, particularly the Skanda Purana. According to legend, Sage Yadarishi, the son of Sage Rishyasringa, performed severe penance inside a cave on this hill. Pleased by his unwavering devotion, Lord Narasimha appeared before him in five divine manifestations and granted his wish to remain on the hill forever for the benefit of future devotees. This divine event gave the hill its name, Yadagirigutta, now popularly known as Yadadri.
legends: Sage Yadarishi, son of Sage Rishyasringa, performed intense penance in a cave on the hill seeking Lord Narasimha's blessings.
Lord Narasimha manifested in five divine forms — Jwala Narasimha, Gandabherunda Narasimha, Yogananda Narasimha, Ugra Narasimha, and Lakshmi Narasimha.
Because the Lord appeared before Sage Yada, the hill came to be known as Yadagirigutta (now Yadadri).

history.content: The temple has been an important center of Vaishnavite worship for several centuries and has received patronage from various South Indian dynasties. In recent years, the Government of Telangana undertook an ambitious reconstruction project, transforming the temple into one of India's grandest spiritual landmarks while preserving its original cave shrine and religious traditions.

sthala_puranam: According to the Skanda Purana, Sage Yadarishi performed intense penance inside a cave on this hill. Pleased with his devotion, Lord Narasimha manifested in five divine forms — Jwala Narasimha, Gandabherunda Narasimha, Yogananda Narasimha, Ugra Narasimha, and Lakshmi Narasimha — and granted the sage's wish to remain on the hill forever. The hill thus became known as Yadagirigutta (the hill of Sage Yada), now called Yadadri.
religious_significance: Yadadri is one of the most sacred Narasimha Kshetrams in India and is revered as one of the holiest Pancha Narasimha Kshetrams. It is a powerful center of Vaishnavite worship where Lord Narasimha is worshipped in five divine forms, each representing a unique aspect of divine protection, compassion, and spiritual power.
spiritual_significance: Devotees believe that worshipping the five manifestations of Lord Narasimha at Yadadri removes fear, protects against negative influences, and brings peace, prosperity, and spiritual fulfillment. The original cave shrine, where Lord Narasimha is believed to have revealed Himself to Sage Yadarishi, is considered especially sacred. Pilgrims visit to seek blessings for health, marriage, education, career growth, business success, and family well-being.

miracles_and_devotee_experiences: Lord Narasimha appeared before Sage Yadarishi in response to his intense penance.
Devotees believe sincere prayers help overcome difficulties, remove fear, and grant relief from health problems, financial hardships, delays in marriage, and family disputes.
Many pilgrims perform Kalyanotsavam, Sudarshana Homam, and Laksha Tulasi Archana after the fulfillment of their wishes.
Devotees describe a profound sense of peace and spiritual fulfillment after visiting the sacred cave shrine.
architecture: Yadadri is one of the finest examples of modern temple architecture inspired by ancient Agama Shastras. The temple has been completely reconstructed using Krishna Shila (black granite) while preserving the sanctity of the original cave shrine. Intricately carved stone pillars, majestic Rajagopurams, beautifully sculpted mandapams, golden Vimanams, and finely detailed sculptures depicting scenes from Hindu scriptures showcase the craftsmanship of traditional temple artisans. The complex spreads across several acres on the hilltop.
architectural_style: Modern temple architecture based on ancient Agama Shastras (traditional South Indian Vaishnavite style)
temple_layout: Main sanctum housing Lord Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy inside the original cave shrine
Shrines for Goddess Lakshmi, Sri Andal, Lord Hanuman, Garuda Alwar, and other Vaishnavite deities

darshan_timings.morning: Temple opens 3:30 AM. Suprabhatam 3:30–4:00 AM; Thiruvaradhana 4:00–4:30 AM; Bala Bogam 4:30–5:15 AM; Nijabhishekam 5:15–6:15 AM; Archana 6:15–7:00 AM. Sarva Darshan 7:00–9:00 AM. VIP Break Darshan 9:00–10:00 AM. Sarva Darshan 10:00–11:45 AM. Nitya Kalyanotsavam 9:45–11:30 AM. Maharaja Bhogam 11:45 AM–12:30 PM. Sarva Darshan 12:30–3:00 PM.
darshan_timings.evening: Dwarabandhanamu (doors closed) 3:00–4:00 PM. VIP Break Darshan 4:00–5:00 PM. Sarva Darshan 5:00–7:00 PM. Thiruvaradhana 7:00–7:30 PM; Archana 7:30–8:15 PM. Sarva Darshan 8:15–9:00 PM. Temple closes after night sevas, typically by 9:45 PM.

darshan_timings.evening: Confirm the same-day board or https://yadagiriguttatemple.telangana.gov.in/timings/ before travelling.

timing_conflict_note: Canonical source is the Telangana Devasthanam timings page (checked 2026-08-21): temple opens 3:30 AM; general Sarva Darshan starts 7:00 AM, not 5:00 AM or 6:00 AM. Older blog summaries that say 5:00 AM–9:00 PM are outdated and must not be used. Timings can change on festival days.

dress_code: Devotees are expected to wear traditional and modest attire. Men are encouraged to wear dhoti, kurta, or formal Indian clothing; women are advised to wear sarees, salwar kameez, or other traditional dresses. Shorts, sleeveless tops, mini-skirts, and revealing clothing are discouraged. Footwear must be removed before entering the temple, silence should be maintained in the sanctum, and photography may be restricted in certain areas, especially near the main deity.
facilities: Shuttle services for elderly devotees and differently-abled visitors

accommodation.availability: Excellent accommodation is provided through Yadadri Temple Guest Houses, Devasthanam Cottages, and TTDC/Temple-managed accommodation complexes. Standard, deluxe, and family rooms are available, along with dormitory facilities for budget travelers.
accommodation.booking_process: Advance online booking is highly recommended via the official ytdtemple.com portal or Devasthanam office, especially during Brahmotsavam, Narasimha Jayanthi, and Vaikuntha Ekadashi, due to the heavy influx of devotees. Walk-in bookings may be available at temple counters based on availability.
accommodation.first_come_basis: Limited walk-in accommodation may be available at temple counters on a first-come basis, but advance online booking is strongly recommended especially during festivals and weekends.
accommodation.price_range: Temple-managed rooms generally cost between ₹300 and ₹1,500 per night, depending on room category and facilities. Dormitory accommodation is available at economical rates. Private hotels and lodges near Yadadri usually charge between ₹800 and ₹4,000 per night.
nearby_options: Private hotels, lodges, resorts, and guest houses near the temple premises

best_time_to_visit: October to March, when the weather is pleasant and ideal for hilltop darshan and sightseeing. Early mornings and evenings offer a peaceful atmosphere. For a spiritually enriching experience, pilgrims prefer visiting during Brahmotsavam, Narasimha Jayanthi, Vaikuntha Ekadashi, Karthika Masam, and Mukkoti Ekadashi.

travel.road: Approximately 65 km from Hyderabad, reachable in about 1.5 to 2 hours. Excellent connectivity via National Highway 163 with regular TSRTC buses, taxis, and private vehicles operating from Hyderabad, Secunderabad, and nearby towns. A well-developed ghat road leads to the hill shrine, with shuttle buses for elderly devotees and families.

reviews.total_reviews: Tripadvisor 'Yadagirigutta Temple' — 4.1/5 across 96 reviews; plus verified reviews from multiple travelers including the older AnjanManda 5/5 review
top_reviews: Tripadvisor (AnjanManda, 5/5): 'Yadagirigutta is a popular Hindu Temple of Sri Lakshminarasimha Swamy, an incarnation Lord Vishnu, situated on a hillock. Being very near to Hyderabad, about 56 kms, it is famous weekend getaway. This is one of the oldest and popular temple of Telangana. The government is proposing to develop the temple in a big way. The nearest railway station is Raigir, 6 KM away. But bus connectivity is very good. Special darshan tickets are priced Rs100 and Rs50. You can cover the temple in 2-3 hours. Generally it is a half day programme from Hyderabad and the road is very good. Devasthanam has limited a/c accommodation and tourism department Haritha hotel is also available. People prefer hotels near Bhongir for breakfast/lunch.'

Tripadvisor (krishna292, 4/5, 'Tirupati of Telangana State'): 'This is a very old temple and draws huge crowds from Hyderabad and nearby areas. Many believers visit it to get their wishes fulfilled. We have been to Yadgirigutta temple about 7-8 years back. It is about 60km from Hyderabad and now takes just 90 minutes for a drive on the recently constructed 4-lane highway. At that time I drove my own car but found very steep curvy road to reach the main temple from the town as it is atop a hill. Then there was a problem in finding a suitable parking pace. So this time when my daughter and her daughter had come from US, I preferred to hire a taxi for visiting the temple. However, I found that a new approach road has been constructed with not so steep upward slope but we were not permitted to take our taxi to the top. Now the temple management has made arrangements for parking the vehicles downhill and for going to the temple one has to either take minibus or an auto-rikshaw (three wheeler). Of course the charges per person are nominal and the ride is good. From the top of hill one gets an excellent view of the country side and town below. We reached the temple at about 9AM within the stipulated timings for free darshan as per the website but were surprised to find that darshan was stopped. Therefore, we had to stand in a que for about 1 hour in an enclosed shed. Then we had to walk through a stony passage uphill for about 15 minutes to reach the main sanctum. The deity here is God Narsimhaswamy, an incarnation of Lord Vishnu with his wife, Goddess Lakshmi. The temple is maintained well and regularly cleaned. From the exit side, prasadam is collected at a marginal price. People should be aware of monkeys. My grand daughter was eating an apple and from some where a monkey came and snatched the apple. I also found another monkey snatching away some one's prasadam. Any resistance can make these monkeys hostile. On the whole it was a good experience. The government is promoting this temple to become another Tirupati of the new state of Telangana after bifurcation from Andhra Pradesh and lot of construction work is going on for accommodation purposes.'

Tripadvisor (tangbot1111, 5/5, 'One of the oldest Temple in Telangana'): 'Yadadri formerly Yadagiri Gutta is the holy place of Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy, Currently, Telangana Govt is expanding the temple and making it as Temple City. A best holy place to visit around Hyd.'

Tripadvisor (Anonymous, 1/5 — critical review, December 2023): 'Visited with family in DEC'23. Overall experience - Horrible... my advise... go with ZERO expectations. Yadadri temple construction had been hyped for the last 5-7 years but the output is like a large money spent with little or no thought for Devotee experience, comfort or convenience. Agreed on religious places, all this is NOT that important and prime importance to be given to Divinity but you also expect basics (if not super top) of convenience, so that you can concentrate on God. Yes. The TRS govt has spent and made the kshetram a presentable one but it is thoroughly mismanaged, corrupt to the core and above all, zero common sense from administration.'

Tripadvisor (Anonymous, mixed): 'This place is easily accessible from Hyderabad. From the hill bottom its just a kilometer distance to the hill top. The place is busy during weekends as it is near to Hyderabad city. It takes 3-4 hours (normal darshan) and 30 mins-1 hour (special darshan 50 rs) during weekend. On weekdays the crowd is bit low and normal darshan will take around 1-2 hours and special darshan (50 rs) take 15-30 minutes. The place is pleasant you can also plan to stay overnight it got plenty of accommodation to accommodate. If going by four wheeler there is a fee of 20.'

introduction.en: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple, popularly known as Yadadri Temple, is a revered Hindu Vaishnavite temple dedicated to Lord Lakshmi Narasimha, the fourth incarnation of Lord Vishnu. Located atop a hill at Yadagirigutta in Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district, Telangana, it is associated with Sage Yadarishi and the divine appearance of Lord Narasimha in five forms. After a grand reconstruction, Yadadri stands as one of India's finest pilgrimage destinations.

history.en: According to the Skanda Purana, Sage Yadarishi performed intense penance in a cave on this hill. Pleased with his devotion, Lord Narasimha appeared in five divine forms and granted his wish to remain on the hill forever, giving the place its name Yadagirigutta, now known as Yadadri. The Government of Telangana recently undertook a major reconstruction, preserving the original cave shrine while rebuilding the temple using Krishna Shila and Agama-based traditional architecture.

travel_guide.en: Yadadri Temple is about 65 kilometres from Hyderabad, reachable in roughly 1.5 to 2 hours via National Highway 163, with regular TSRTC buses, taxis, and private vehicles. The nearest railway station is Raigir, about 5 kilometres away, and the nearest airport is Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad, about 90 kilometres away. The temple opens at 3:30 AM; general darshan typically starts at 7:00 AM. Pilgrims should confirm today's board on the official Devasthanam timings page, carry water, and book accommodation in advance during festivals.

faq.question: Where is Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple located?
faq.answer: The temple is located at Yadadri (Yadagirigutta), Yadadri Bhuvanagiri District, Telangana, about 65 km from Hyderabad.

faq.question: Which deity is worshipped in the temple?
faq.answer: The temple is dedicated to Lord Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy, the fourth incarnation of Lord Vishnu.

faq.question: Why is Yadadri Temple famous?
faq.answer: The temple is famous for the five manifestations of Lord Narasimha, its sacred cave shrine, and its magnificent reconstruction based on traditional temple architecture.

faq.question: What are the temple timings?
faq.answer: According to the Telangana Devasthanam timings board, the temple opens at 3:30 AM with Suprabhatam. General (Sarva) darshan is typically 7:00–9:00 AM, 10:00–11:45 AM, 12:30–3:00 PM, 5:00–7:00 PM and 8:15–9:00 PM. Doors are closed 3:00–4:00 PM (Dwarabandhanamu). The temple closes after night sevas, usually by 9:45 PM. Confirm on https://yadagiriguttatemple.telangana.gov.in/timings/ before you go. Do not use older blog hours such as 5:00 AM–9:00 PM.

faq.question: Is there an entry fee for darshan?
faq.answer: No. Sarva Darshan is free for all devotees. Paid options such as Seegra Darshan, VIP Break Darshan, and various Arjitha Sevas may also be available; confirm current fees at the counter.

faq.question: Which is the biggest festival celebrated here?
faq.answer: Brahmotsavam is the grandest festival celebrated at Yadadri. Narasimha Jayanthi, Vaikuntha Ekadashi, and Mukkoti Ekadashi are also celebrated with great devotion.

faq.question: Are accommodation facilities available?
faq.answer: Yes. Temple guest houses, Devasthanam cottages, dormitories, and numerous private hotels are available near the temple.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Yadadri Temple?
faq.answer: The ideal time to visit is between October and March, especially during Brahmotsavam, Narasimha Jayanthi, and Vaikuntha Ekadashi.
